strengths.home: Drew all five UNL games this cycle and need a win to go up; only Croatia have beaten them at home since 2024. Have scored in all but one of the last 13. Davidsen often scores penalties.
strengths.away: Beat Kazakhstan 2-1 and a draw may be enough to progress; none of their five games stood level at half-time. Popescu has 5 goals in 5 games but gets booked often. No injury worries.

AmO1Tbim.synopsis: Faroe Islands must win to go up but have drawn every game; the writer still suggests a sixth straight draw.

strengths.home: Bottom of Group C3, winless in the UNL since 2022; leaky (2 conceded in each of last 4), only one defeat in 6 home games. Seven straight games with both teams scoring; Samorodov suspended.
strengths.away: Back in League B, scored 11 UNL goals (7 before half-time) and committed a group-low 39 fouls. Haraslin has lost only one of 10 internationals he scored in. No fresh injuries.

CUwHKU8F.synopsis: Two sides that attack well but defend poorly; the writer picks both teams to score.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in the UNL (W2, D3), four straight clean sheets, no goal conceded after the hour in 10 matches; strong at home. Still has an outside chance of automatic promotion.
strengths.away: Lost 5-0 to Iceland and finish a poor campaign; only 2 of last 8 games saw both teams score. Petkov scores early. Estonia have never scored against them in three meetings.

0hNdxfzI.synopsis: Estonia's solid defence and motivation against a demoralised Bulgaria; the writer backs Estonia to win to nil.

strengths.home: Group leaders, unbeaten (W3, D2), 12 scored and 1 conceded, 5-0 win in Bulgaria; a draw likely enough for top spot. Oskarsson scores early. Two players hurt in the last game.
strengths.away: Conceded 7 of 8 UNL goals before half-time; only one of last 14 games had both teams score. Dardari scores first when he scores. Tim Hall a doubt.

6sMHTP3t.synopsis: Iceland need only a draw and have the better record; the writer likes Iceland in the half-time/full-time market.

strengths.home: Won the reverse 2-0 and five of seven H2Hs were 2-0; clean sheet in 7 of last 8 wins. But 0-0 under a caretaker coach, scoreless in 7 of last 12, and lead striker Kucys plus three others out.
strengths.away: Seven straight games under 2.5 goals, five 2-0 losses; failed to score in 15 of 17 defeats. Captain Hasler absent; Saglam their last scorer in a win.

QaWOXbQr.synopsis: Lithuania are favourites on H2H and form despite absences; the writer calls a 2-0 Lithuania win ambitious but plausible.

strengths.home: Six wins in the last seven at home (four clean sheets), beat Serbia 3-1; need a result to progress. Gruda in form (7 goal involvements in 9). No fresh injuries.
strengths.away: Hammered Greece 7-0 with a Reijnders hat-trick; need to avoid defeat to go through. Led at half-time in only two of the last five and rarely booked.

2RA7BZ1C.synopsis: Group decider in Berlin; Germany have the greater need. The writer prefers the Germany/Draw double chance.

strengths.home: Lost 7-0 to the Netherlands, failed to score in two games and hasn't won in several; top two still possible. Pavlidis in form at club level. No new absentees.
strengths.away: Nine of last ten games over 2.5 goals and both teams scoring in five of six, but Dragojevic and Zivkovic are suspended and their away record is poor. Tadic back in form.

YgNbVTho.synopsis: Greece are shaky after the 7-0 but Serbia are depleted and weak away; the writer backs a Greece win.

strengths.home: Already top of the group; four clean sheets, five straight home wins, scored 2+ in each of last three in St. Gallen. Manzambi out injured.
strengths.away: Beat North Macedonia 2-1 and must win to stay in promotion hunt; six clean sheets in last seven away games. Robertson set to become their most-capped player. Binks and Welsh withdrew.

2VjYW7HL.synopsis: Switzerland are through while Scotland need a win; the writer finds Scotland/Draw (double chance) tempting.

strengths.home: Winless this cycle (D2, L1), scored once, failed to score in 8 of 11 home games but unbeaten in four at home with three clean sheets. Jolley doubtful.
strengths.away: Seven points from nine and close to winning the group; only 2 of last 9 UNL games had both teams score. Mbong and Scanlon-type scoring threats; no fresh injuries.

rsY1QVmI.synopsis: Malta in form against a goal-shy Gibraltar; the writer backs Malta to win and keep a clean sheet.

strengths.home: Winless in 13 (D5, L8), lost the last six, finish bottom; only 3 of last 14 games saw both teams score. Bardhi scores at home.
strengths.away: Held Switzerland 0-0 but failed to score before half-time in 9 of 11 UNL games; Bijol suspended. Vipotnik is an away specialist.

O6zXDY9j.synopsis: Two low-scoring sides; the writer's pick is under 2.5 goals.
